title: Salmon Sushi Bake
equipment: 8×8-inch metal or ceramic baking dish (not glass, since it goes under the broiler)

items: 1½ cups sushi rice (short-grain), rinsed until the water runs clear
Kosher salt and black pepper, to taste
¼ cup Japanese mayo (such as Kewpie)
3 packs roasted seaweed snack sheets (about 30 sheets)

steps: Combine the rinsed rice and 1¾ cups water in the saucepan. Bring to a boil over high heat, cover, turn the heat to low and cook 15 min. Take it off the heat and let it steam, still covered, 10 min.
Meanwhile, heat the oven to 400°F with a rack in the middle. Stir the rice vinegar, sugar and 1 tsp salt in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Set the salmon on a foil-lined sheet pan, rub it with the oil and season lightly with salt and pepper. Bake 12–15 min, until it flakes easily and reads 145°F in the thickest part. Leave the oven on.

Pour the vinegar mixture over the hot rice and fold it in with a spatula, cutting through rather than stirring so the grains stay whole. Press the rice evenly into the baking dish and sprinkle with the furikake.
Flake the salmon with a fork. Mix it with the cream cheese, ¼ cup mayo and sriracha to taste until evenly combined.
Spread the salmon mixture over the rice in an even layer. Bake 10 min, until hot all the way through.
Switch the oven to broil on high and broil 2–3 min, until the top browns in spots. Watch closely, since mayo burns fast.
Stir the 3 Tbsp mayo and 1 Tbsp sriracha together and drizzle over the top in lines. Scatter with scallions. Scoop onto seaweed sheets and add a slice of avocado and cucumber to each bite.
tips: Make it ahead: spread the salmon mixture over the rice (step 6) but don't bake it. Cover and chill up to 1 day, then bake 20 min at 400°F and broil.
Leftover cooked salmon works here. Skip step 3 and use about 2 cups flaked salmon.
No Kewpie? Use regular mayo with 1 tsp rice vinegar stirred in.
storage: Best the day it's made. Fridge up to 2 days, covered, with the avocado and cucumber kept separate. Reheat at 350°F for 10–15 min or in the microwave 1–2 min. Don't freeze.
